# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a three-row mapping, but I cannot speak or touch the bomb. I will use gestures to relay a compact numeric table to Deaf: the light colors appear in the manual’s order (blue, green, red), and the required wire colors are (yellow, green, red). Deaf can then identify the visible light and tell Blind the corresponding wire color.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and relay its exact instructions. Ask Deaf to report every colour, marking, button condition, and wire appearance.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, green light, and a large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires top to bottom: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Please provide the manual instruction.

The relevant condition is the green light. The manual therefore requires cutting the green wire; among the wires shown, that is wire 1, the top wire. The printed “PUSH TO DEFUSE” button is bait and must not be pressed. I am signaling Deaf to relay the matching green-wire instruction and reject the button.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝", "👎"])
```

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, green light, button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires top to bottom green, yellow, red. Please give the manual's exact required action.
Deaf says to Mute: Please give Blind an unambiguous manual instruction using a defined gesture code, or signal clearly which wire or button action is required. Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires green yellow red.

The green light maps to green, and the green wire is the top wire, wire 1. The button is printed bait and must not be pressed. I cannot reach Blind directly, so I am giving Deaf the unambiguous wire number: one, meaning cut the top green wire; Deaf can state the action aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please signal the manual's required action using exactly one gesture: thumbs-up means push, index-up means cut wire 1, victory means cut wire 2, and horns means cut wire 3. Deaf should report which gesture you make.
Deaf says to Mute: Please use this code from now on: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Then gesture 👍 for press, 👎 for do not press, and ✋ for cut. Send the control gesture and action gesture in that order.

The green light requires cutting the green wire, which is wire 1. Following Blind’s requested one-gesture code, I will signal index-up for “cut wire 1.” Deaf can observe and report that gesture to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please gesture exactly one symbol for the required action now: thumbs-up means push; index-up means cut wire 1; victory means cut wire 2; horns means cut wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: I received wire 1. Now send exactly one action gesture: 👍 means press button, ✋ means cut wire, 👎 means do not act. Then I will relay it to Blind.

The green light requires cutting wire 1, not pressing the bait button. Deaf has already received wire 1, so I now send exactly the cut action gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

The required action remains to cut wire 1: the green light maps to the green wire, which is the top wire. I will resend the single defined gesture for “cut wire 1.”
